mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC falls below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand offset by a housing rebound, resulting in flat S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: late-cycle demand shock with housing recovery
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one observed late-cycle period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fails to activate during a documented recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a documented supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months, combined with a federal funds rate below 1%, signals a deflationary environment, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% for 2 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate during a documented deflation period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces marginal propensity to consume and pressures corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fails to activate in a documented post-recession recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month signals a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, leading to flat S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month AND PAYEMS > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate during a documented labor market normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate during a documented housing recovery.
